caption: The drawing depicts three objects arranged side by side against a plain, off-white background. From left to right, there are two standing human-like dolls and a brightly colored bag with a smaller doll inside. The first doll (on the left) is the largest, dressed in a long red cape with a green edge, decorated with white and purple trim, and has a head covering consisting of green and red fabric bands. The doll’s face is brown and featureless with black hair, and its arms are crossed over the chest. The second doll (center) is slightly shorter, clothed in a red cape with a green-edged hem, a blue garment underneath, a necklace, and a head covering with brown hair peeking out. Its right arm is bent toward the chest and legs are dressed in multicolored, vertically striped cloth. The third object (right) is a bag, featuring vertical sections of green, yellow, red, and blue, with two dark maroon handles. Inside the bag, a small doll is visible, dressed in colorful cloth and a pink head covering. Each item has vivid coloring and a mix of patterns, emphasizing textile details. There are small, faint letters “A,” “B,” and “C” beneath each object.
title: Indian Dolls
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
